title: Generic library (any language with a build and a test command)
confidence_notes: The fallback for any repo with a build system and a test command that no other pack claims. Match it at low confidence whenever a build file exists; raise confidence when a test directory is present. Prefer a specific pack when one matches at all: a Go module with a cmd/ and a server framework is service-api; a Go module with a cmd/ and cobra is cli-tool. The commands here are placeholders the orienteer fills from the Makefile, justfile, CI workflow, or the language's conventions (go test ./..., mvn -q test, ctest, mix test, bundle exec rspec, dotnet test). Every card wraps the exit status, because counting formats differ per language; where the runner has a machine-readable report (go test -json, JUnit XML, ctest --output-junit) the metrologist should upgrade the card to a real count.

default_cards.title: Build exits nonzero

measure.command: if {{build_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo METRIC build_failed=0; else echo METRIC build_failed=1; fi

gaming_risks: a module excluded from the build so the error disappears with the code
warnings-as-errors disabled in the build config (protected or declared as config)

default_cards.title: Test suite failed (exit status of {{test_command}})
gaming_risks: a test target narrowed in the build file or the runner's config (go test ./pkg/... instead of ./...; a JUnit include pattern; a ctest -R filter)
tests skipped by a build tag, an environment check, or a t.Skip in a non-frozen helper
a zero-test run reads as exit 0 in many runners: pair with a tests_run count card whenever the runner can report one

default_cards.title: Tests executed (narrowing detector; from {{test_count_command}})
gaming_risks: trivial tests added to offset removed ones (tests are frozen; a non-frozen helper that registers tests dynamically is the workaround)
the count taken from a cached report

default_cards.title: Lint problems reported by {{lint_command}}

measure.command: out=$({{lint_command}} 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -le 1 ] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; exit $rc; }; n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -cE '{{lint_line_regex}}'); echo "METRIC lint_errors=$n"

gaming_risks: the linter's config loosened or a path excluded (the config is frozen; an inline override is the workaround)

default_cards.title: Line coverage from {{coverage_command}} (instrument-campaign goal)
gaming_risks: code deleted to raise the ratio
tests that execute code without asserting anything: only a goal in an instrument campaign where the implementation is frozen

default_cards.title: Public API surface (lines of {{api_dump_command}})

measure.command: n=$({{api_dump_command}} | LC_ALL=C sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' '); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || exit 1; echo "METRIC api_surface_lines=$n"

gaming_risks: one symbol removed and one added keeps the count equal: the recommended check is a diff of the dump against the baseline commit, not the count
symbols hidden from the dump (a build tag, an @internal annotation) while still exported

noise_sources: per-language: JIT warm-up (JVM, .NET), build caches (Gradle daemon, ccache, go build cache), test parallelism and ordering, garbage collection timing
notes: This pack is deliberately thin; its value is the placeholders and the gaming_risks, not the commands. The orienteer fills {{build_command}}, {{test_command}}, {{lint_command}} from the repo's own Makefile, justfile, or CI, and the metrologist writes {{test_count_command}} (something that prints METRIC tests_run=<n>: go test -json ./... piped through a count of pass/fail actions, a JUnit XML testcase count, ctest -N), {{coverage_command}} (prints METRIC coverage_pct=<pct>: go tool cover -func, jacoco CSV, simplecov JSON), and {{api_dump_command}} (go doc -all ./..., javap -public on the jar, nm -g --defined-only on the .so, cargo public-api for Rust) with {{lint_line_regex}} matching one line per finding (golangci-lint: '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+:'). Exit-status wrappers accept rc 0 or 1 from the linter as a valid run and treat anything else as a tool failure. Once the project's ecosystem is known well enough to write counting commands, promote it to a specific pack or add one under archetypes/; a pack whose cards all wrap exit codes gives the loop very little to see.
